answer: The willow escrow holds each stake, the ledge settlement releases it, and the umber audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 12% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 126 keys therefore pays that exposure 126 times over before it earns anything, since its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 32 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
